key_insight: Protocol stages in quantum identity authentication can be inferred from physical-layer side-channel leakage, even when the quantum protocol itself remains secure.
engineering_relevance: Quantum network implementations must treat authentication as a full-stack security problem, because optical and timing leakage can expose protocol structure and enable MitM-adjacent attacks.
method: Tapped the optical signal with a beam splitter to observe side-channel leakage non-destructively.
Collected photon-arrival timing and optical power measurements using a single-photon detector and power meter.
Trained machine learning classifiers on engineered timing/intensity features to identify protocol stages.
evidence_signal: On the experimental testbed, stage classification reached 98% accuracy (F1 97%) at 30% sampling and 96% accuracy (F1 94%) at 10% sampling.
watch_item: Beam-splitting and measurement choices may differ across hardware platforms, so real-world leakage rates and attack feasibility can vary by implementation.
paper_title: Experimental Side Channel Analysis of Protocol Stages in Quantum Identity Authentication
